title: A geometric connected component covers a connected locally algebraic scheme
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $K/k$ be an algebraic closure [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $X$ be a nonempty connected scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme] locally of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Put $Z=(X\times_k\operatorname{Spec}K)_{\mathrm{red}}$, using affine spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] and scheme reduction [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. A connected component means a maximal nonempty connected subset. Then $Z$ has finitely many irreducible components and has a nonempty connected component. Every connected component $Y$ of $Z$ is open and closed in $Z$. With its open subscheme structure, $Y$ is a nonempty connected reduced scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme] locally of finite type over $K$, has finitely many irreducible components, and the composite $p:Y\hookrightarrow Z\to X$ is surjective on underlying points.

proof.text: Write $W=X\times_k\operatorname{Spec}K$, with projection $r$. List the finitely many irreducible components of $X$ as $T_1,\ldots,T_m$. They cover $X$. By the finite-preimage lemma each $r^{-1}(T_i)$ is a finite nonempty union of irreducible components of $W$. Together these give a finite cover of $W$ by irreducible components. Any other irreducible component $C$ is contained in one member of this cover: intersect the finite closed cover with $C$ and use irreducibility, successively. Maximality then forces equality. Thus $W$ has only finitely many irreducible components. The reduction immersion $Z\to W$ is a homeomorphism: it is a closed immersion and is the identity on underlying sets. Therefore the same finiteness holds for $Z$.
The map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is surjective; its base change $r$ is surjective as well. Since $X$ is nonempty, $W$ and hence its reduction $Z$ are nonempty.

Here is the finite topological argument giving the components of $Z$. Join two of its finitely many irreducible components when they meet, and partition the components by chains of such intersections. An irreducible space is connected: a nontrivial clopen partition would express it as two proper closed subsets. The union belonging to each chain class is connected, since a clopen partition would put each irreducible member on one side and intersections force the same side along every chain. Each union and its complement are finite unions of closed irreducible components, so it is clopen. These unions cover $Z$ and are disjoint; a connected subset meeting one cannot meet its complement. Consequently they are exactly the maximal nonempty connected subsets. There is at least one by nonemptiness. Fix any such component $Y$. Its irreducible components are exactly the irreducible components of $Z$ in its class: a maximal irreducible subset of $Y$ lies in an ambient component by the covering lemma, that ambient component lies wholly in this clopen $Y$, and maximality gives equality. In particular $Y$ has finitely many irreducible components.

source.place: Tag 004W (lemma-irreducible), closedness and covering; elementary finite-intersection-chain argument supplying the clopen components used in Tag 04L7

proof.text: Give $Y$ its open subscheme structure. The reduced-induced-subscheme theorem applied to the full closed set $|W|$ says that $Z=W_{\mathrm{red}}$ is reduced. The local rings of an open subscheme are the same as those of its ambient scheme, so $Y$ is reduced. To verify local finite type without assuming quasi-compactness, take the affine cover $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ of $X$ from the definition, with each $A_i$ generated by finitely many elements over $k$. Its base change has affine charts $\operatorname{Spec}(A_i\otimes_k K)$. Reduction replaces each coordinate ring by $B_i=(A_i\otimes_k K)/\sqrt{0}$, still generated over $K$ by the images of those generators. Every point of $Y$ in this chart has a principal neighbourhood $D(f)$ contained in $Y$: write the closed complement in $\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ as $V(I)$ and choose $f\in I$ outside the prime of that point. Such a neighbourhood is affine with coordinate ring $(B_i)_f$, by the affine principal-open lemma. This algebra is generated by the finite generators of $B_i$ together with $f^{-1}$. These neighbourhoods cover $Y$, proving local finite type over $K$.

The projection $r:W\to X$ is open by the universally-open-over-a-field lemma, applied to $\operatorname{Spec}K$ over $k$ and base scheme $X$. It is closed as well: $K/k$ is algebraic, so every element of $K$ satisfies a monic polynomial over $k$ after division by the leading coefficient. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is integral by the affine definition. Its base change $r$ is integral, hence universally closed and in particular closed. Under the reduction homeomorphism $|Z|=|W|$, the subset $Y$ is nonempty, open and closed, so $r(Y)$ is a nonempty clopen subset of $X$. Connectedness of $X$ forces $r(Y)=X$. This is exactly surjectivity of the composite $p:Y\hookrightarrow Z\to X$.
